After three hours I have to say, this game is an absolute slog. Pros: -nice pixel art characters & map (I've only seen one, in 3 hours) -interesting addition of missions to the genre -interactive map features -low cost Cons: -snail in molasses move speed for mc & mobs (why does it have to be like this) -incredibly under-powered early game with all but 1 character -even maxed out in meta-progression, exp pick-up radius is tiny -very confusing hit-boxes (everyone making these games needs to learn from Binding of Isaac, use the character shadows as the hit-box) -very stingy with items (character has 10 item slots, I've never had a run with more than 3 active items, again, three hours of game-play. I've only ever seen 4 active items total so maybe there are only a few in the game right now) -I've had 1 crash & had the game freeze twice, have not experienced this in other games in the genre -leveling up feels much less impactful than in other similar games (WHERE IS MY DOPAMINE!!) -no item evolution's, as far as I can tell. I've fully leveled up almost every characters starting weapon & the end result was just a slightly faster, VERY SLIGHTLY more damaging, same kinda boring weapon. -stingy meta-progression currency drops -not terribly exciting meta-progression unlocks Final notes. If the first few minutes of each run did't feel like such a chore I probably would've been much more forgiving of the other faults I find in the game. My experience playing this has more or less been as follows, slog my way through the first few mins trying desperately to pick up enough exp to keep up with the encroaching mobs & avoid taking too much dumb damage, getting the exp but failing to not get hit 7 times due to the aforementioned confusing hit-boxes, running away to get apples or health fountains, not keeping up with mob scaling due to running for health, running out of healing, getting to the boss with a maxed out feather duster and an ice wand that doesn't really seem to do anything and dying because the boss either doesn't take damage or one shots me. Not super fun so far. I may check back for updates but there are a lot of games like this to choose from...

This is almost a good game but it's not and it's incredibly frustrating instead. The Good: - The system by which there are interact-able tiles and missions is very interesting and something this genre desperately needs. - I highly appreciate runs are only 15 minutes instead of the traditional 30. The Bad: The main issue is regarding the monster damage and the player health. There are few ways to recover health, and even fewer ways to mitigate damage, there are no ways to block projectiles, yet the monsters do HUGE amounts of damage late in a run. I have had MULTIPLE runs where I have gotten to 14:30 (game ends at 15:00), where my build is completely obliterating everything on the screen, only to be 1 or 2 shot by a projectile (and its ALWAYS A PROJECTILE that kills you). It doesn't even matter if you are constantly clearing the screen of monsters, because projectiles will fly from off-screen and the entire screen is constantly obscured from massive damage text popups, HUGE popup text indicating events, your own projectiles and explosions, your own summons, etc. There you are, finally assembled a good build, shooting 50 arrows per second, lightning bolts flying, meteor explosions going off, your summons protecting you from the mass of incoming monsters, experience and coins flying across the screen into your character. The visibility is terrible, which is not uncommon for this genre of game, but what is unique to this game is the lack of balance and defense tools to deal with this. So, what happens is, after you've finally spent several runs learning how to build the character and getting lucky with drops, you finally get late into a run and are close to winning, some elite mob will spawn with the projectile ability and when they are just on the edge of your screen they fire a little sinister fire ball, and you cant see it, because your screen is covered in unimportant garbage, and the only thing you need to care about, that little orange devil ball, is completely lost among the sea of colors and flashes, and that little hell orb touches your character, and then, boom, the game is over. Play better next time, noob. Making the character get reduced to 1 hp when they take critical damage is not the solution. Monster damage and player health need to be re-balanced. Monsters do WAY TOO MUCH DAMAGE. Some other criticisms: - Having a ton of skulls but not being able to pick more powers because of the power cap based on monster kills feels TERRIBLE and is completely pointless. Especially because it means that if you want to play different characters, you have to constantly go back to that screen and sell powers and buy ones that synergize better with the character you are playing. The number of powers you have access to is already balanced by how many skulls you have, this additional layer of max powers is completely unnecessary, its existence PROVIDES NO VALUE and only serves to frustrate the user. - The auto aim is bugged. Auto aim is completely broken for melee attacks and regularly attacks not the closest monster and also always at the wrong angle. Auto aim for projectiles is broken and while the "main" or "first" projectiles target the closest enemy, the "2nd" projectile will aim at your mouse but with a 5 or 10 degree offset. It is very obviously bugged just play mage and get 2 projectiles. - The controls in this game feel like they were created by someone who has never played a video game before. Left click to use consumable? Scroll wheel to move between consumables? The default controls on a controller are even more horrendous. I didn't even bother trying to remap them because you would literally have to change every bind for it to make sense. - The "air attacks" are really annoying. These need to be telegraphed better. In the games that this mechanic was copied from, they indicate which side of the screen the monsters are about to come from and when they are coming much better. It also feels like most of the characters just need to burn their ability to not take damage from this, which is bad design because late game when everything does so much damage, if you are not playing summoner (who doesn't care about air attacks because you just sit in a mass of your minions and they kill everything coming at you), you have to always hold your ability in preparation of a potential air attack. It's not telegraphed enough, most characters don't have passive ways of dealing with it, and it means you can never use your ability offensively. There are some good ideas here, but it feels like every system in this game is implemented slightly wrong.

[i]Horde Hunters is your standard VS like at its core, but it delivers a much more active experience than others in the genre. You’ll be hunting down items and resources, interacting with various buildings as required, and completing missions for additional rewards. Long gone are the days where you create an overpowered build and idle while wave after wave is obliterated immediately.[/i] [table] [tr] [th]Category[/th] [th]Rating[/th] [th]Description[/th] [/tr] [tr] [td]🎮 Gameplay[/td] [td]5[/td] [td]The introduction of interactible buildings and missions is nice, but gameplay is held back by high monster damage, slow movement, and an overall lack of rewarding progress [/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]📷 Graphics[/td] [td]7.5[/td] [td]Well executed pixel art, although the font, and scale of interactables and the interface could be improved[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]💲 Value[/td] [td]8[/td] [td]A no brainer if you’re a fan of the genre[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td] 😇 Overall[/td] [td]6.5[/td] [td]An interesting take on VS likes, changing up the formula enough to make it feel fresh, but it’s lacking that dopamine hit due to how unrewarding it feels[/td] [/tr] [/table] [h1]📝 Main Pros, Cons, and Suggestions:[/h1] 🟩 Pros: + Usable items + Active abilities + Customisable difficulty + 7 Characters and 4 Maps + 200% game speed (7.5 min rounds) + Customisable characters (colour palette) + Much more active gameplay compared to other VS likes + Interactable buildings, with unique missions, in each stage will change how you play 🟥 Cons: - Monster damage and player health feel imbalanced (it's frustrating) - Meta progression doesn’t feel rewarding - Similar can be said for levelling up - Game speed impacts everything (enemy movement and projectiles), not just the game clock (I expected this, but some may not like the added difficulty) 🏷️ Suggestions: ~ Rework monster damage, particularly ranged projectiles ~ Increase the benefits gained during level up along with the meta progression, I want to feel powerful [h1]An Active VS Like[/h1] Horde Hunters is an interesting and a unique take on the genre. Personally, I loved the bank and the tower buildings the most. The bank lets your deposit your gold to earn interest, giving you more power later at the risk of having less power now. The tower is much simpler but very useful, especially later in the game, as the additional firepower could mean the difference between death or survival. Additionally, having abilities and items really mixes things up. I know other VS likes have done this too, but Horde Hunters does it better (at least for items, in my opinion). Instead of immediately being consumed/used, you hold onto them, and can activate them when necessary. Not only that, but you can search for and collect what you need, which is another welcomed change. [h1]It’s Refreshing[/h1] Horde Hunters is a refreshing take on the genre, and a welcomed one at that. If you’re new to the genre, I recommend looking at more established titles first, but for existing fans, you will enjoy the different direction the game takes. It feels early in development, but with enough community feedback, I’m confident that this could become one of the greats. I enjoyed this game thoroughly and it was a great addition to the survivor-like genre with its own unique twist in the form of the "towns" or structures/events strewn across the landscape. I also really enjoyed the ability to change the default attack of each character as well as their abilities, making for very personalised builds and playstyles. If you're carving your way through the survivor-like genre like I am and you're trying to get another hit of that sweet survivor dopamine, this game has a lot of unique ideas to offer and its worth a play. Definitely a hidden gem, with a developer who clearly cares and responded to my bug submission AND dropped a hotfix within 12h of my report.

[b][h1]Horde Hunters[/h1][/b]Having played a lot of other bullet-heavens, I expected a pretty cut-and-dried experience going into this, but Horde Hunters does not play like any other games in the genre. HH takes a more methodical approach to runs, where it benefits you to play it slow, pause and plan your route through the map, this along with balancing collecting items and keeping a good economy for upgrades makes for fairly difficult runs. [b][h2]Gameplay[/h2][/b]There's a good variety of characters currently, each being either melee, ranger or magic, these all have different starting stats, items, abilities and unique weapons. You can customise their main attack and abilities with various buffs and debuffs depending on the playstyle or build you plan on doing. All characters can be upgraded by killing enemies allowing you to allocate points to upgrade their starting stats. The two main things that make this game stand out are the character stats and economy, all characters have stats like Strength, Agility, Luck, etc, that affect various gameplay elements, you can upgrade these as you level up getting bigger bonuses for reaching 50% and 100% in each stat. Economy is what really sets this game apart as you don't just level up and get stronger as you also have to collect coins to be able to purchase the stats and weapon upgrades at every level-up. There are a few maps to choose from with different gameplay elements across them all like different buildings, areas that slow you down and elements that can hurt you, the maps themselves are good. However every map uses the same enemies, elites and final boss fight against elites, it'd be a lot more appealing if each map had enemies visually specific to that map or elites with unique attacks. The ending boss fight to each run is just more elites, which feels a little lacklustre, I think it would be cool if each map had their own boss that you had to plan your items around in advance. On top of character levelling you also have a typical meta-progression where you can equip up to 10 different Power-ups that buff various stats and gameplay events, you can mix and match these depending on which map and character you play as. You are able to directly change the health, damage, speed and number of enemies with the difficulty modifiers from 50% up to 150% allowing for dynamic difficulty depending on how good you are, runs are short at only 15 minutes, but you are also able to set the game speed faster to speed up runs to 7.5 minutes. This game has endless maps where you can fight for a highscore, the higher your difficulty, the higher your score multiplier. With the nature of leaderboards the game is balanced around scaling until you die, so it doesn't really feel endless, my only real issue with the game is that you never really feel strong, it always feels like enemies catch up to you. Weapons have endless upgrades at max but they are so miniscule at +1% damage that it rarely ever feels impactful, my personal suggestion would be to raise the buffs these endless upgrades give you but have the prices raise with each additional level, this means you also need a good economy and would help keep endless leaderboards balanced. [b][h2]Achievements (93/93)[/h2][/b]The achievements are not too difficult once you learn the game and you'll collect meta-upgrades which will make them easier as you play. Each map in-game shows which achievements you are missing which can be useful. [b][h2]Settings/Accessibility/Misc[/h2][/b]You can transfer your save file from the demo. Lots of useful settings for gameplay. Option for different cursor style/colour as well as a projectile transparency slider helping with visibility. Supports keyboard, mouse and gamepad with control rebinding. Only English language supported currently. [b][h2]TL;DR[/h2][/b]Methodical bullet-heaven that stands out in the genre. Short runs, 15 minutes or less. Missions to complete on each map. Level up characters permanently by killing enemies. Modifiable difficulty. Leaderboards for endless score grinding. Lacks enemy variety. Fairly easy achievements. [quote][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/39729435-JHG-Reviews/?appid=2218750]Check out my Curator page[/url][/quote]

When Horde Hunters left early access I posted a long organized review detailing the good and bad, but then the dev kept updating the game and addressing the leftover cons so I removed my pointless review. Basically completing simple objectives works great in a survivors-like and it seems the dev really tried to make a fun game that was both innovative and good. A con is that the graphics are weak in many places but the gameplay and build customization make up for them. Difficulty is customizable but it can be high on normal+ because i-frame grace period after getting hit is a mere 1/6 of a second. It's difficult to see certain attacks[strike], especially bomb enemies that have no AoE indicator after they die[/strike]. (Dev added an indicator and other nice improvements in an update.) There are a few unusual design choices (like the interface), but they are easy enough to understand and don't cause me problems. I'm glad I tried this and wouldn't recommend sleeping on this one if you are interested in being more involved in your survivors-like gameplay.

A really fun Vampire Survivor-like game with some cool twists. Progression feels great. Every run gives you something to build on, and it’s actually rewarding instead of just grindy. I love that there are missions to complete during your runs. It gives you a reason to think beyond just “stay alive” and makes each session feel more purposeful. There’s also a good variety of weapons, so you’re not stuck doing the same thing every time. You get to experiment a lot, and some combos are really satisfying to pull off. The game manages to be challenging without being frustrating. It keeps you on your toes, but it doesn’t feel unfair or overwhelming. If you like the Vampire Survivor style but want something with a little more structure and variety, this one is definitely worth checking out.

Gave this a positive review despite feeling like it's a 4/10 even in just its own niche. If you've played any Survivors-like, this is the same except all the weapons are of the type you'd expect to start with in Rust-likes. What I mean to say is: the bow shoots arrows, the spike ball spins around you, the sword does a melee arc swing, and all the summons just kinda follow you around. It's not _terrible_, but the lack of content and interesting builds makes this a slog. It feels more tedious than fun, and it never truly rewards you for growth besides your runs getting smoother. There's 5-10 maps, 5-10 characters, and 5-10 weapons. Go play 20 Minutes Till Dawn instead.
It's... not that fun? It wants to be unique, but it ends up just being frustrating.

Highly recommended! On the surface it looks like a VS-type survival/bullet-heaven game, but there are SO many more layers. So many. You need to plan and adapt more than turn off your brain and 'get in the pocket' to win at this game. No knock to those zone-out type games (love them) but this game isn't that. Knowing when you use what items, how to level up (that's right, how you do it is critical), how to find synergies, immediate and lasting improvements, what quests to attempt and what ones might be too tough for your character and just what the heck is going on with all the variables it critical. Fortunately, the game is fun to play, albeit a BIT too grindy at first, and knowledge comes over time. Try some wacky stuff just to see what they do and you might find your favorites mix. It is slower paced than many of the entries similar to this, but that thoughtfulness is a feature in this case. Closer to an ARPG than a straight VS-type game, but 100% enjoyable and worthwhile.
